endorsements.quote: To improve performance and efficiency, selected AI tools or algorithms, with the highest ROI, must be seamlessly integrated into the Radiology workflow and reporting systems to achieve the greatest impact.

Despite the “black box” nature of AI, it is essential that there be full disclosure of the use of AI and its limitations and benefits to all stakeholders (administrators), actors (Radiologists), and beneficiaries (patients).

However, ideally, a sandbox of superusers needs to fully investigate a new application before implementation.
Proven clinical performance, stringent clinical validation, and fiscal evaluation that consider the tangible and intangible financial impact must be undertaken.

unlisted_practices: Validate and scrutinize the performance of AI tools before adoption.
Evaluate the fiscal return on investment, both tangible and intangible, of AI tools before adoption.
Keep radiologists in the loop as the final decision-maker rather than deploying autonomous AI until AI demonstrates clinical judgment and documented superiority over humans.
Pair AI-assisted detection of incidental findings with patient navigators and follow-up programs to ensure appropriate follow-up care.
Have diagnostic radiology leaders engaged in clinical research and product evaluation evaluate available AI tools prospectively and retrospectively.

screen.reason: Editorial describing institutional experience and providing recommendations/frameworks for selecting and financially justifying AI applications in radiology.
